findings.status: source-established behavior; intended coupling remains an owner policy question
findings.producer_to_consumer: Public Shell::set_collision_surface installs obstacle positions/faces/clearance solely into private SurfaceContacts. In positive-interval interleaved stepping, project_host_contacts calls that entire solver only if public self_collision.enabled is true. Therefore an installed fixed triangle-surface route is skipped when that self-collision flag is false.
findings.conditions: Installed fixed surface, a positive host interval and iterations, self_collision.enabled false. Separate Collisions GPU/outer-layer routes may be configured and remain available; this trace does not claim all collision is absent or decide whether coupling is intended.
findings.historical_relationship: Q-L12-a6453dca0eb01ea0a5da already records no-self-collision as a legitimate mode and preserves the host schedule; the interaction with separately installed fixed triangles is a specific conditional owner/policy question, not an automatic distinct global finding. Earlier RIG-PPS-023 traces the static clearance producer through Shell/SurfaceContacts. No source change in the three ordered bodies.
findings.future_repair_direction: Decide explicit authority for fixed obstacle processing versus cloth self-collision; if independent, route/control the fixed-surface path separately while preserving zero host interval, optional outer layer, prescribed masses, and separately configured GPU colliders. Verify caller expectations later.

findings.producer_to_consumer: With nonempty static_positions, public solve copies the caller inverse masses, appends static positions, then resizes the mass vector to the combined length using PINNED before solve_inner asserts lengths. A missing dynamic mass is padded as prescribed; extra supplied masses up to the obstacle count are interpreted as dynamic masses for static vertices, and still more are truncated. Thus the inner equal-length check sees the transformed vector rather than the input mismatch.
findings.conditions: Malformed direct-public solve call with inverse_masses length unequal to dynamic positions length and at least one static position; actual input validity and impact depend on caller. Dynamic entries supplied by the ordinary ShellMesh construction route are already length-checked. No runtime or native-buffer mismatch claimed.
findings.historical_relationship: Related to SEGOVB-L12-CONNECTED-SURFACE-SOLVE-MASS-EXTENT-ADMISSION, READ-L12-774 and Q-L12-ecc1905cee4fdbdbbfa9: these record the inner equal-length assertion. The pre-assert static-surface resize is a distinct first-failure facet, not proof of an unrelated canonical owner; reconcile centrally rather than duplicate automatically.
findings.future_repair_direction: At the public dynamic aggregate boundary, check positions, previous, masses, retained topology and representable static extent before appending exactly prescribed static masses; preserve intentional static zero mass, ordinary valid mode, and direct API invalid-input policy. Check all producers and error ownership later.

findings.status: source-established conditional public-state divergence, historically recorded
findings.producer_to_consumer: Shell::new validates mesh then clones triangles into both public Shell.triangles and private SurfaceContacts. Public mutation or replacing public particles can break their relation; read_mesh directly indexes read-back positions with current public triangle indices, and outer-layer projection consumes that public list while surface contacts retain original faces.
findings.conditions: After successful construction, caller mutates/replaces public state. Out-of-range triangle can panic if the readback succeeds; a valid changed list can be inconsistent with retained solver topology. No unsupported claim that canonical constructor admits invalid indices.
findings.historical_relationship: Explicitly recorded in READ-L12-772 and Q-L12-a6453dca0eb01ea0a5da. Our bounded read supplies the previously requested actual mesh validator: its initial face and seam membership checks protect Shell::new. Preserve history and connect this retained-state mutation facet, rather than inventing a duplicate.
findings.future_repair_direction: Assign one authoritative admitted topology/particle extent or a coordinated mutation operation that rebuilds all affected retained consumers; preserve mesh export and collision behavior for valid topology.

findings.status: source-level mathematical counterexample to internal sweep contract; actual end-to-end impact remains open
findings.producer_to_consumer: Internal CCD first samples initial separation, then returns None when maximum relative displacement is at most 1e-15, even when nonzero movement closes the initial clearance gap. All inputs and clearance in the example below are finite f32; ShellMaterial permits any positive finite thickness, and the surface solve admits positive finite thickness.
findings.symbolic_example: For a stationary triangle with vertices (-1,-1,0), (1,-1,0), (0,1,0), move its interior point vertically from z=3·2^-53 to z=−3·2^-53. Let clearance be 2·2^-53 (thickness 4·2^-53). The initial distance is 3·2^-53 > clearance, relative travel is 6·2^-53 < 1e-15, and the point passes through z=0; the stated branch returns None. This is mathematical source reasoning, not a constructed/run fixture.
findings.conditions: Very small representable world-space scale, unrestricted by the examined local finite/positive admission. It establishes a missed private sweep event, not an observed missed surface collision: resolve deliberately falls back to end proximity after None and can still project. Actual allowed physical scale, broad-phase and full-consumer policy require further review.
findings.historical_relationship: Q-L12-a6453dca0eb01ea0a5da names exact zero speed as intentional and says no numerical proof was established. A nonzero movement under the hard cutoff is not the same as exact zero; do not overwrite that historical claim or assert a historical reviewer ran this example. Earlier RIG-PPS-023 preserved CCD safe-budget behavior and precision requirements.
findings.future_repair_direction: Either prove and enforce an admitted scale-relative/no-crossing speed bound tied to the actual gap, or maintain conservative sweep behavior for any representable nonzero displacement; preserve true zero speed, finite budgets returning Some(last safe contact), degenerate geometry and proximity policy.

findings.status: source-level conditional numerical under-resolution; geometric-domain policy open
findings.producer_to_consumer: For nonzero nearly parallel edges, the determinant threshold forces the first segment parameter s=0. That endpoint-only selection can overestimate the true separation when the closest points lie inside both segments. The resulting estimate is also the CCD initial distance.
findings.symbolic_example: Let e=2^-48, z=2^-60; edges A=(0,0,0) to B=(1,0,0) and C=(0,-e/2,z) to D=(1,e/2,z). All components are f32-representable. Their true closest distance is z at their midpoints. The source determinant is e²=2^-96 < 1e-28·aa·cc with aa≈cc≈1, so it sets s=0 and obtains separation approximately e/2, much larger than z. With stationary edges and clearance 2^-55, the sample exceeds clearance and the zero-speed branch returns None, though true separation is below clearance. Mathematical reasoning only; no fixture or numeric program was run.
findings.conditions: Extremely near-parallel nondegenerate geometry; no general claim that a physically supported garment can or does reach this regime. Geometric centerlines do not intersect, but configured contact shells overlap initially; the SurfaceContacts untangled-start policy may restrict intended use. The endpoint fallback and coupled contacts need separate consumer proof.
findings.historical_relationship: Older Q-L12-a6453dca0eb01ea0a5da preserves explicit degenerate-edge and finite-fallback modes but does not prove nearest-point accuracy for nonzero near-parallel edges; no whole-family conclusion or evidence transfer.
findings.future_repair_direction: Prove or constrain an acceptable scale/angle/contact error bound and ensure an overestimate cannot invalidate conservative advancement; preserve legitimate degenerate and parallel cases.

lens_perspectives.name: producer propagation
lens_perspectives.assessment: Static clearance remains raw through Shell setter and SurfaceContacts to sweep; earlier RIG-PPS-023 distinguished missing owner from observed checked-value stripping. Contact masses are typed but the aggregate length is not protected before static resize. No full producer inventory.

lens_perspectives.name: existing owners
lens_perspectives.assessment: Earlier RIG-PPS-023 names a possible shared NonnegativeLength owner for static clearance; its zero/removal mode differs from positive-finite runtime thickness. Verify exact current owner and rejection behavior rather than assuming one checked owner fits both.

lens_perspectives.name: admission
lens_perspectives.assessment: ShellMesh validates initial particle count, face/seam membership and masses. Public SurfaceContacts boundaries retain documented assertions and lack dynamic mass precheck in static branch; historical direct-API errors remain distinct from normal constructor.

lens_perspectives.name: invariant operations
lens_perspectives.assessment: CCD nonzero speed threshold and near-parallel approximation have symbolic conditional counterexamples; their surface-consumer consequences and admitted physical scales remain unproved. Budget exhaustion returns Some and is not a miss.

lens_perspectives.name: aggregate states
lens_perspectives.assessment: Public topology and particle replacement can diverge from private contact faces; static solve changes mass lengths before the aggregate assertion. Initial mesh validation does not protect later public mutation.

lens_perspectives.name: type ownership
lens_perspectives.assessment: SurfaceContacts owns retained geometry and separate static clearance, Shell exposes contact policy through SelfCollision.enabled; resolve policy and actor ownership before assigning repair. Supplier rig was an audit source assignment, not a transfer of product ownership.

lens_perspectives.name: redundant authority
lens_perspectives.assessment: Public Shell.triangles and private SurfaceContacts.faces are independent stored copies after construction. Static fixed bounds are intentionally rebuilt on replacement; no automatic stale-cache finding for a valid replacement.

lens_perspectives.name: behavior preservation
lens_perspectives.assessment: Preserve zero host interval GPU-only path, optional outer layer, zero static clearance/removal, finite-budget conservative result, exact zero/prescribed inverse mass and valid degenerate geometry; no runtime parity conclusion.

lens_perspectives.name: enum shapes
lens_perspectives.assessment: A public self-collision boolean also gates fixed-surface host processing; decide whether these are independent policy states. An enum alone does not repair ignored or divergent state.

lens_perspectives.name: derivability
lens_perspectives.assessment: HostContactSchedule already derives ordinary equality/copy traits. No necessary manual-boilerplate elimination established in this bounded scope.

lens_perspectives.name: type granularity
lens_perspectives.assessment: Static nonnegative clearance (including zero) and positive finite simulated thickness have different policies; count/index/extent relate across topology and state. Avoid conflating those concepts or f64 arithmetic internals with admitted owner invariants.

lens_perspectives.name: raw strings
lens_perspectives.assessment: Retain the 059 distinct interval count and admission-reason findings; Shell no-particles error is downstream unreachable at the current mesh validator. Do not treat every prose error as a new unique cause.

lens_perspectives.name: raw primitives
lens_perspectives.assessment: The 1e-15 and 1e-28 numerical thresholds are equation-specific and their bounds are unresolved; schedule counts intentionally include zero/max policies, geometric vectors are native math operands. No blanket literal replacement.

nonfindings_and_open_questions: A fixed surface replacement reconstructs and commits the cached bounds; no unqualified stale-obstacle-on-replacement finding. Source tests show intent only and were not run.

Zero host interval explicitly selects GPU-only contact scheduling; zero iterations and nonpositive/nonfinite thickness have defined no-contact behavior at the inspected boundary. Whether these policies are correct for each actual producer remains open.
CCD budget exhaustion returns the last conservative contact as Some, not None; exact zero relative speed is distinct from the positive threshold example.
Positions/velocities GPU writes are sequential in project_particles; native write failure behavior and retry policy were not inspected, so do not claim a partial-commit defect.

Checked huge particle count, offset representability, finite fixed obstacle input, cross-particle input membership, execution domains, real scales, WGSL behavior and all native error consumers require separate registered inspection. No runtime, numerical execution or shader behavior was checked.

No physical intersection/tunneling assertion follows solely from the internal sweep counterexample because resolve calls proximity. No ordinary invalid face/seam claim follows for Shell::new because mesh.validate checks them first.
